subject: Novapulse request: targeted 90d debug/session log retention — definitional Q&A
messages:
From: Claire Hudson <claire.hudson@novapulse.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@novapulse.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug/session logs — Novapulse tenant

Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're doing a risk review for a new product line and our compliance team is asking whether Redwood can accommodate a limited exception to the standard 30‑day debug/session log TTL for a subset of customer events. Specifically: we need 90 days retention for transaction correlation traces and full debug snapshots for a defined set of tenant IDs tied to clinical workflows.

Questions we need to resolve before we sign a scoped addendum:
- Can Redwood place a tenant‑scoped retention tag (90d) on session/debug logs for a defined tenant subset?
- What artifacts/evidence can you provide to demonstrate retention and subsequent deletion (SOC 2 / CAIQ expectations — proof of delete, signed manifests, chain-of-custody)?
- Will there be any constraints (e.g., ephemeral caches, KV cache, or memory-only traces) that cannot be extended?
- If this is possible, what is the typical lead time and what approvals (security/legal/billing) do you need?

I've attached a short doc outlining Novapulse's ask and the list of tenant IDs we intend to include. We're aiming to have contractual language by mid‑October if feasible.

Best,
Claire Hudson
Director, Security & Compliance
Novapulse Health
Attachments: novapulse-req-90d.pdf

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug/session logs — Novapulse tenant

Karthik — I looked through the ask and sketched a feasible path. TL;DR: Hosted can support a tenant‑scoped 90d retention for persistent session/debug logs with caveats; deliverable evidence will require an evidence-gathering runbook and signed artifacts from Security.

Technical summary:
- Retention tagging: we have per-tenant metadata tags on our logging pipeline (ingestion -> object store lifecycle) that can extend TTLs at artifact level (S3 or object-store shard) for session and debug logs. We can implement a 90d lifecycle policy scoped to the tenant prefix.
- Ephemeral data: KV cache and runtime-only traces (in GPU memory, transient LRU buffers) are not persisted and cannot be extended. We need to enumerate which Novapulse artifacts are considered "persisted logs" vs "ephemeral runtime state."
- Forensics/export: we can provide a secure export (encrypted tarball) of the retained logs on request and a signed deletion manifest when TTL expires or when we execute a manual delete.

Evidence we can reasonably provide (examples):
1) Erase manifest: machine-generated manifest with object keys, deletion timestamps, operator id.
2) Signed timestamp: Security signs the manifest (PKI) and we include S3 object delete markers.
3) Audit trail dump: ingestion IDs, retention-tag assignment logs, and deletion job run logs.
4) Hash chain: per-batch SHA256 for retained objects to show provenance prior to deletion.

Estimated lead time & approvals:
- Implementation (config + test): 4–7 business days to enable retention tags and verify export flows in a dev tenant.
- Evidence runbook and template: 3 business days for Security to review and sign a standard artifact template.
- End-to-end delivery: 10 business days from approval to first signed proof-of-delete (for a one-off initial export + manifest).

Ops notes / constraints:
- Hosted is fine for this scope; Dedicated/Private is not required unless Novapulse requires stricter network isolation or custom retention tooling.
- There may be a one-time operational surcharge to cover retention storage and evidence packaging (~pricing tbd with Sales/Billing).

I've attached a short playbook and an evidence artifact template to use as starting points.
Attachments: retention-playbook-v2.pdf, evidence-artifact-template.docx

Happy to join a call with Novapulse if you want me there.

— Priyom
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: 90d targeted retention for debug/session logs — Novapulse tenant

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and the tenant list. After an internal review (summary below) we can support a tenant‑scoped 90‑day retention exception for persisted session/debug logs with a formal MAP and evidence package.

What we propose (summary):
- Scope: apply 90d retention to persisted session logs and debug snapshots for the tenant prefixes you provided. This does NOT extend in‑memory KV cache or ephemeral GPU runtime traces. We'll work with you to classify which artifacts are in/out.
- Deliverables: initial signed evidence package after the first deletion cycle including: signed erase manifest (operator + timestamp + keys), ingestion/retention assignment audit logs, S3 delete markers, and per-batch SHA256 provenance list. We will also provide quarterly attestations for the duration of the exception.
- Timeline: pending internal approvals (Security + Legal + Billing), we estimate 10 business days to produce the first signed proof-of-delete after Novapulse approves the MAP. Enabling the retention tag and smoke tests: 4–7 business days.
- Approvals & pricing: this requires Security signoff (for the evidence format) and Legal for contract addendum language; Billing will propose a small storage/ops surcharge.

Next steps we suggest:
1) We draft a short MAP (I've attached a draft) that lists tenant IDs, data classes, acceptance criteria, and timelines.
2) Quick 30‑minute sync (this week) to confirm artifact classes and any SLA expectations.
3) Once Novapulse approves MAP, Redwood will route through Security/Legal and begin implementation.

I've attached: a draft MAP, the retention playbook, and the evidence artifact template for your review. Also linking a Jira ticket we opened to track approvals: JIRA-SEC-1124.

Would you be available for a call Thursday or Friday?

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference
